deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes from about 1981 on arrangements K of N pseudolines in the projective plane. The neighbouring pages are autobiographical German text, unrelated to the mathematics. Grothendieck has defined a family of 'degenerate' types on earlier pages. The page only partly fixes their meaning.

- I_N, I_{p,q}, II_N are the arrangements in which two vertices meet every pseudoline, i.e. all lines pass through one of two points (pencil and near-pencil-like cases).
- II_4 is the case N=4 that is not degenerate in another way. Most plausibly it is 4 lines in general position, the complete quadrilateral: two opposite vertices of it cover all 4 lines.
- I'_{3,2} and II_5 are small 'forbidden' subarrangements on 5 lines, defined on earlier pages. They are not recoverable with certainty from this page.

Theorem (excluded-subconfiguration classification). Suppose K is not of type I_N, I_{p,q}, II_N, and contains no subarrangement of type II_5. Then K is one of the following (the list was enlarged in a later addition):
- III_6, the 'tetrahedral' arrangement. These are the 6 lines of a complete quadrangle, i.e. the A_3 reflection arrangement, projectivised. It has 4 triple points plus 3 double (diagonal) points, giving 4+3=7 vertices.
- IV_7, 'a quadrilateral and its three diagonals'. That is 4 lines in general position plus the 3 lines joining opposite vertices; equivalently, a complete quadrangle plus one line through two of its diagonal points. It has 6 triple points plus 3 double points, giving 6+3=9 vertices. Check: 4 quadrangle points and 2 diagonal points become triple; the third diagonal point and 2 new intersections are double. This is Grünbaum's simplicial arrangement A(7,1) (the 'near-Fano' configuration). The figure circles the diagonal points and dashes the added lines.
- A later addition also lists I_{2,2} (quadrilateral plus 1 diagonal) and I_N (N≥5).

NB (corollary). Every arrangement 'without bigon' is one of two things:
- of type II_4, or
- contains one of I'_{3,2}, II_5, III_6.

If it contains neither I'_{3,2} nor II_5, it is III_6 or IV_7. In the projective plane a 2-gon face occurs essentially only for pencils, so 'sans bigone' means non-trivial.

The three types I'_{3,2}, II_5, III_6 are called 'latticiels'. In dimension 2 this means the closed cells of the induced cell decomposition of P^2 form a lattice: the intersection of two closed faces, if non-empty, is again a closed face (cell). This is an intersection property of the CW complex, i.e. it is 'polyhedral-like'. The page breaks off mid-sentence.

Purpose: these three are the minimal non-degenerate arrangements, which every non-trivial arrangement contains. The aim is presumably to study arrangements whose face complex has good combinatorial (lattice/regularity) properties, as part of a programme on the combinatorial topology of pseudoline arrangements (moduli of 'systèmes de pseudo-droites').
errors: The theorem as first written lists only III_6 and IV_7. Grothendieck then had to add I_{2,2} and I_N (N≥5) in a marginal correction, so the original statement was incomplete; the hypotheses on excluded degenerate types need care.
The meaning of II_5, I'_{3,2} and of the degenerate families depends on definitions on earlier pages. Without them the completeness of the list cannot be verified from this page alone.
The claim that I'_{3,2}, II_5, III_6 are 'latticiels' is asserted without proof here, and the definition is cut off at the page end.

ideas.what: Classification of non-degenerate pseudoline arrangements by minimal forbidden subarrangements: every non-trivial arrangement contains one of a few small types
ideas.modern_name: Excluded sub-arrangement / minimal non-near-pencil arrangements; Ramsey-type results for pseudoline arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Background from Levi (1926), Grünbaum (Arrangements and Spreads, 1972), Goodman–Pollack (1980s); no specific credited statement of this form known

ideas.what: Tetrahedral arrangement III_6 (complete quadrangle, 4 triple + 3 double points)
ideas.modern_name: A(6,1), projectivised A_3 reflection arrangement / braid arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Grünbaum catalogue of simplicial arrangements

ideas.what: IV_7: quadrilateral with its three diagonals (6 triple + 3 double points)
'Latticiel' arrangements: the closed faces of the cell decomposition form a lattice (two non-disjoint closed cells meet in a single closed cell)
ideas.modern_name: Intersection property / regular CW (polyhedral) cell complex; face lattice of an oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face lattices of oriented matroids: Folkman–Lawrence (1978), Edmonds–Mandel; Björner et al., Oriented Matroids (1993)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a structure theorem: every non-trivial pseudoline arrangement contains one of three minimal 'latticial' subarrangements (I'_{3,2}, II_5, III_6), and those avoiding the first two are exactly III_6 and IV_7. This links an excluded-configuration classification to a property of the face complex (closed cells forming a lattice). I know of no published statement of exactly this characterization of minimal arrangements with lattice face complexes.
missed.quote: Tout arrangement sans bigone, soit est du type II_4, soit contient un des types I'_{3,2}, II_5, III_6 ... Ces trois types sont "latticiels"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Questions of when the cell complex of a projective arrangement has the intersection property (regular vs. polyhedral) are of interest in oriented matroid theory and the topology of arrangements. A minimal-obstruction description would be a small but citable combinatorial lemma; it is likely easy to reprove, so its novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: It is a genuine, unpublished small classification theorem by Grothendieck in pseudoline-arrangement combinatorics, a field he never published in. Its content (A(6,1), A(7,1), near-pencils) is elementary and close to known Grünbaum/Goodman–Pollack material, so a specialist would find it charming rather than surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'Arrangement tétraédral' is written over a struck-out first attempt ('Arrangement' crossed and rewritten).
The marginal addition reads approximately '... ou I_{2,2} (quadrilatère + 1 diagonale) et I_N (N≥5)', written in a bracket to the right of the second figure.
NB line: after 'sont les' a word ('configurations') is struck out and something like 'seuls arrangements avec' seems intended before 'N≥5'; uncertain.
The second figure's caption reads 'Arrangement d'un quadrilatère et de ses trois diagonales'; the dashed lines in the figure are the added diagonals, and the circled points are diagonal points.
